lines.en: How could someone get a hold of your credit card number?
I have no idea, but look how much they spent.
The credit card people said you only have to pay for the stuff that you bought.
Still, it's just such reckless spending.
I think when somebody steals your credit card,
they've kind of already thrown caution to the wind.
Oh, Monica, you are not still going over that thing.
She's living my life, and she's doing it better than me.
She buys tickets to plays that I want to see.
She buys clothes at stores that I'm intimidated by the salespeople.
Yeah, well, I might be if I had the supplies.
I mean, I could do all this stuff.
Oh, it's so late for shall we.
Do I go horseback riding in the park?
Do I take classes at the new school?
She's got everything I want, and she doesn't have my mother.
Uh, yes, this is Monica Geller.
Um, I believe I'm taking some classes with you, and I was wondering what they were.
What, what, so that you can dance with the woman that stole your credit card?
I should get to see who she is.
Okay, Monica, you know what, honey?
You're kind of losing it here.
I mean, this is really becoming like a weird obsession thing.
It's madness, I tell you, for the love of God.
Which one do you think she is?
You don't observe a dance class.
I think she means you dance.
Come on, come on, come on.
Hey, you see anybody you think it'd be me?
People, last time there were some empty yoga containers lying around after class.
Let's not have that happen again.
So, who's the new tense girl?
I spent three years in Amsterdam.
Yeah, I like this dance, honey.
Where the hell have you been?
Mike and I just crash an embassy party.
They want to know if you're going to be showing up for work.
Going to the Big Apple Circus today.
Okay, Monica, what are you doing?
You're going to lose your job.
You know, I'm not just the person who needs to fluff the pillows
and pay the bills as soon as they come in.
You know, when I'm with her, I am so much more than that.
